extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, third-party requesters, patent examiners, and their attorneys/agents handling inter partes reexamination appeals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/content requirements for taking appeals and cross-appeals, and for preparing appellant and respondent briefs, in inter partes reexamination proceedings before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (per MPEP §§2674–2675.01). Covers timing, form, content, admission of amendments/evidence, and consequences of noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) prerequisite and filing window
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal cannot be taken by parties to the reexamination until a Right of Appeal Notice (RAN) has been issued. Once RAN issued, patent owner and any third party requester have one month or thirty days (whichever is longer) to file a notice of appeal with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for filing a notice of appeal may not be extended (37 CFR 41.61(e)). If no timely notice of appeal is filed by any party, prosecution terminates and the examiner issues a Notice of Intent to Issue Inter Partes Reexamination Certificate (NIRC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and signature requirements for notice of appeal/cross appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of appeal or cross appeal must identify the appealed claim(s) and must be signed by the owner, the requester, or a duly authorized attorney or agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a notice of appeal or cross appeal is timely filed but noncompliant (e.g., missing fee, unsigned, missing proof of service, failure to identify appealed claims), the appropriate party will be notified and given a non-extendable time period to file an amended notice; failure to correct results in dismissal of that appeal (37 CFR 41.61(f)). Form PTOL-2067 should be used to provide the notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of appeal (from which determinations appeal must be taken)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal or cross appeal must be taken from all the rejections of the claims in a Right of Appeal Notice which the patent owner proposes to contest or from all the determinations favorable to patentability (including any final determination not to make a proposed rejection) in a RAN which a requester proposes to contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester appealing an allowance must identify each previously proposed rejection it intends to contest — merely appealing the allowance is insufficient. Questions unrelated to merits may be required to be settled before an appeal is decided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-appeal timing and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Within fourteen days of service of a requester’s notice of appeal an owner who has not filed may file a notice of cross appeal (and vice versa within 14 days of service of an owner’s notice). The 14-day cross-appeal period may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 41.61(b) provides for cross appeal from a 'notice of appeal' not from a 'notice of cross appeal.' In multi-requester merged proceedings, cross-appeal timing may run from an earlier owner appeal rather than a later requester appeal. If a cross appeal is timely but defective, one opportunity to amend within a non-extendable one-month period is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to correct defective notices but non-extendable deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: If a timely notice of appeal or cross appeal does not comply with requirements, appellant will be notified of reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time period to file an amended notice; failure to file an amended notice that cures the defects results in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a notice of appeal or cross appeal is filed before a RAN is issued it will be placed in the file but not considered; the party will be notified that the appeal is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board responsibility for determining brief compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board has sole responsibility for determining whether appeal briefs comply with 37 CFR 1.943(c) and 37 CFR 41.67, 41.68, or 41.71, and will complete that determination before forwarding briefs to the examiner for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board finds a brief non-compliant it will send a notice requiring a corrected brief; if compliant (or contains only minor informalities) the Board accepts it and forwards it. Once accepted by the Board, a brief will not later be held defective by the CRU or examiner or cause a remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing appellant's brief (non-extendable)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must be filed no later than two months from the latest filing date of the last-filed notice of appeal or cross appeal, or two months from expiration of the time for filing such notice if a party entitled to file fails to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The time for filing an appellant's brief or an amended appellant's brief may not be extended (37 CFR 41.66(a)). Failure to timely file the brief and requisite fee will result in dismissal of that appellant's appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's brief required contents (37 CFR 41.67(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant’s brief must contain, under appropriate headings and in order: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals/interferences/trials; (iii) Status of claims; (iv) Status of amendments; (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (concise explanation referring to specification columns/lines and drawings; identify means-plus-function elements per 35 U.S.C.112(f) with corresponding structure/material/acts); (vi) Issues to be reviewed on appeal; (vii) Argument (contentions on each issue with citations); (viii) Claims appendix; (ix) Evidence appendix; (x) Related proceedings appendix; (xi) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item must be present and complete. For (v), for dependent claims argued separately, identify means/step-plus-function items and corresponding disclosure with page/line and drawing references. The evidence appendix must contain only evidence entered into the record (no reference to unentered evidence). A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment/affidavit/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including new or non-admitted amendments or evidence in briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s or respondent’s brief shall not include any new or non-admitted (non-entered) amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence (37 CFR 41.67(c)(2) and 41.68(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.63 and 1.116 for the narrow circumstances under which amendments or affidavits/evidence filed after filing an appeal may be admitted (e.g., cancellation of claims that do not affect scope; reopening prosecution under 41.77(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and consequences when brief is non-compliant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a filed brief does not comply with 37 CFR 41.67(a) and (c), appellant will be notified of reasons and given a non-extendable one-month period to file an amended brief. Failure to correct defects results in dismissal of the appeal; if an appellant brief is late, respondent brief will be placed in file but marked 'not entered' and not considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where all parties who filed appeals fail to timely file an appellant brief and fee within the time allowed, the reexamination proceeding is terminated by NIRC and a certificate is issued indicating claim status at time of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and content requirements for claim appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims appendix must contain a copy of the claims to be reviewed on appeal. The copy should be a clean copy including all brackets and underlining as required by 37 CFR 1.530(d) to reflect changes made during reexamination; any new claims must be completely underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For convenience, the copy of the claims should start on a new page and be double spaced. The copy must reflect bracketing/underlining of claim changes throughout prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument presentation and waiver rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument must present the appellant’s contentions on each issue with citation of statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the record. Each issue must be treated under a separate heading. If the patent owner groups multiple claims under a ground rather than arguing them separately, the Board may select a single claim from the group to decide the appeal; failure to separately argue grouped claims constitutes waiver of separate patentability arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement merely pointing out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument. Arguments or authorities not included in the brief (or in permitted respondent/rebuttal briefs) will be refused consideration unless good cause is shown. Oral argument will not cure deficiencies in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidence appendix must contain copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to 37 CFR §§1.130, 1.131, or 1.132 or any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by the appellant/respondent, together with a statement where in the record that evidence was entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted in the brief. See §41.63 for treatment of evidence submitted after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent brief limitations and required contents (37 CFR 41.68)
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent’s brief must be limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which the respondent brief is directed. It must be signed, accompanied by the requisite fee, and contain under appropriate headings: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals/interferences/trials; (iii) Status of claims (accept or dispute appellant’s statement specifying errors with particularity if disputed); (iv) Status of amendments (accept/dispute); (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (accept/dispute); (vi) Issues to be reviewed on appeal (accept/dispute; may include counter-statement); (vii) Argument (accept/dispute appellant contentions with citations); (viii) Evidence appendix; (ix) Related proceedings appendix; (x) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester’s respondent brief may not address any brief of any other requester. A respondent brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing respondent's brief (non-extendable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appellant’s brief has been properly filed, any respondent must file a respondent brief within one month from the date of service of the appellant’s brief. The time for filing a respondent’s brief or an amended respondent’s brief may not be extended (37 CFR 41.66(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file may have procedural consequences; the respondent brief may be placed in the file but marked 'not entered' if procedural timing is defective for the appellant side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of amendments, affidavits, declarations, or exhibits after appeal filing (37 CFR 41.63)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after filing an appeal that cancel claims may be admitted where such cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim. All other amendments filed after filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted where patent owner reopens prosecution under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1). Affidavits or other evidence filed after filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted where prosecution is reopened under 37 CFR 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner desires an amendment or evidence during appeal stage, the examiner must reopen prosecution, accept the amendment/evidence for entry, permit timely comment by third-party requester, and then issue a new Action Closing Prosecution (ACP) (see MPEP §2673.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and signature requirements for briefs
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s or respondent’s brief must be signed by the party or the party’s duly authorized attorney or agent and must be accompanied by the requisite fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to include the fee (or other essential formality) can render the notice/brief defective but timely-filed defective matters permit a single non-extendable opportunity to correct defects; use Form PTOL-2067 for notifications of defective filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failing to file timely appeal-related papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a party fails to file a timely notice of appeal or cross appeal, that party may no longer file an appellant brief to appeal a claim determination adverse to that party. If all parties who filed an appeal fail to timely file an appellant brief and fee, the reexamination proceeding is terminated and an NIRC is issued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring or acquiescing in any rejection or determination (including correctable formal matters) will invite dismissal of the appeal as to the appropriate party. Prosecution is considered terminated as of the date of dismissal of all appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of appeal papers filed before RAN or other procedural anomalies
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of appeal or notice of cross appeal is filed before a RAN has been issued, the appropriate party will be notified in writing that the appeal is not acceptable; the paper will be placed in the file but not considered in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, the Board (not the examiner/CRU) will determine compliance of briefs; examiners should no longer hold appeal briefs defective that the Board has already reviewed and accepted.
